tradeoffs.J01: SELECT: primary adjusted-utility leader. Original-H&E-conducted appearance is the best aggregate compromise. Native BCSS25 confirms false gold rims and TIGER23 still loses thin stroma; shared lumen filling remains. Retain as leader, not a uniformly correct anatomical result.
tradeoffs.L02: SELECT: second adjusted utility. Adds predictive appearance variance with almost unchanged aggregate IoU and some case-specific border improvements, but no gain over J01 (150 wins,155 losses,44 ties). All319 informative cases clip negative stochastic diagonal estimates; uncertainty is approximate and uncalibrated. Retain a prospectively distinct hypothesis for replacement by better numerical models.
tradeoffs.K05: SELECT: third adjusted utility and strongest raw accuracy among the selected five. Bending regularity preserves some narrower tissue separations that J01 merges. It is slower,29 images exceed one second, and false gold rims and vessel/fat confusion persist. No claim of dominance over J01.
tradeoffs.L03: SELECT: fourth adjusted utility; retains exactly J01 tissue decisions except additional H&E glass deletion. Actual BCSS54 and native BCSS07 show real cleft opening, but many internal lumina stay filled and positive-reference deletions lower IoU (12 wins,132 losses,205 ties). Keep this explicit background mechanism for improvement, not as an accuracy success.
tradeoffs.C17: SELECT: fifth adjusted utility and distinct direct palette inverse. Removes false gold rims in annotated native BCSS25 and grey fringes in BCSS60, but can erase small structures and still fills lumina. Its affine direct pixel inverse differs from the quantized/prior-regularized palette children; complete implementations, not loss-only ablations, are compared.
tradeoffs.J07: REJECT from next roster: fast Gaussian hinge model, but below the five retained utility values and shared thin-structure losses persist.35 informative-case optimizers terminate unsuccessfully. False gold rims in BCSS129 and false satellites remain despite useful individual cases.
tradeoffs.K13: REJECT from next roster: fast empirical-noise exponential risk lies below the selected five in accuracy/utility.22 informative-case optimizer failures and false islands/fringes remain; retained only in immutable history as a comparator.
tradeoffs.L01: REJECT: nonlocal H&E graph lowers parent IoU,65 wins versus252 losses and32 ties, while increasing runtime. Contact sheets show rougher and fragmented edges without recovering fine networks; stain similarity can transport appearance between unrelated regions.
tradeoffs.L04: REJECT: all349 native masks are byte-identical to K05; all947 constrained fits terminate at zero iterations because bounds are inactive. Extra runtime has no output benefit. A distinct mathematical hypothesis did not yield a distinct solution on this corpus.
tradeoffs.L05: REJECT: radial-Huber bending lowers K05 mean IoU slightly and substantially increases runtime,169 images over one second.61 cases contain a nonconverged nested fit. Fine lumen and septal errors persist; tiny local changes do not justify cost.
tradeoffs.L06: REJECT despite highest raw mean IoU: improvement over J01 is only0.11966 IoU percentage points at1.9414 seconds mean and258 images over one second. Covariance eigenvalue clipping occurs on all319 informative cases. Some branches improve, but many lumina and fine structures stay wrong and utility is far below survivors.
tradeoffs.L07: REJECT: Hellinger palette implementation lowers C17 IoU,102 wins versus215 losses, and adds grey fringes in native TIGER23 and BCSS74/86. Five cases have unconverged fits. Affine quantization and prior also differ from C17, so do not attribute failure to divergence alone.
tradeoffs.L08: REJECT: heavy-tailed palette fit lowers C17 IoU,97 wins versus219 losses;20 cases are not converged. Grey fringes and erased thin tissue persist. Nonconvex downweighting of large colour discrepancies has no general benefit in the complete implementation.
tradeoffs.L09: REJECT: minimum-entropy mixture lowers C17 IoU,100 wins versus217 losses;158 cases fail the outer convergence criterion. Purifying fractions does not recover anatomy and grey fringes persist. No proof that finite majorization reaches the optimum.
tradeoffs.L10: REJECT: joint-rival cubature hinge is slightly worse than J07 and below retained utility.52 optimizers terminate unsuccessfully,maximum gradient0.1103. Fine strands remain lost and false satellites/fringes persist.
tradeoffs.L11: REJECT: tile-specific uncertainty gains just0.01231 IoU percentage points over J07,107 wins versus183 losses.48 optimizer failures exceed parent35. It remains below all five selected utility values and does not resolve anatomical errors.
tradeoffs.L12: REJECT: kernel class-distribution distance lowers J07 mean IoU by0.84717 points,85 wins versus231 losses. Grey/gold fringes are visible in many BCSS/TIGER interfaces and thin structures are not recovered. Nonlinearity alone is not a useful improvement.
tradeoffs.L13: REJECT: upper-quarter CVaR lowers K13 mean IoU,98 wins versus215 losses.106 optimizers terminate unsuccessfully,maximum gradient0.5529. Some fringe suppression is offset by rougher islands and sensitivity to difficult coarse labels.
tradeoffs.L14: REJECT: row/column correlated-noise law lowers K13 IoU,109 wins versus172 losses,with24 optimizer failures. Fast output is not sufficient: false fringes and lost branches persist, and lower utility gives no survivor slot.
tradeoffs.L15: REJECT: equal-tile log risk has zero unsuccessful optimizer flags and is fast, but lowers K13 IoU,100 wins versus209 losses. Improved numerical stopping does not overcome lower accuracy and unresolved false islands and thin-structure losses.
